title: Advanced Runtime and Deployment Compilation
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of advanced runtime and deployment compilation in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply advanced runtime and deployment compilation to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: Advanced Runtime and Deployment Compilation is lesson 179 in Performance, Memory, and Low-Level C#. .NET supplies the runtime, SDK, and libraries around C#. The compiler typically emits intermediate language and metadata; runtime compilation or ahead-of-time publishing determines how native code is produced.
content.why_it_matters: Optimization should begin with measurement and should preserve safety, correctness, and portability. This lesson focuses on advanced runtime and deployment compilation and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates advanced runtime and deployment compilation. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates advanced runtime and deployment compilation rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for advanced runtime and deployment compilation before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.
content.expected_output: Publish settings affect startup, size, compatibility, and reflection behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
